metadata.title: The Cross-Medium Conformance Suite
metadata.note: One declaration, two renderings, one law -- S13b, the keystone. The assertion is NOT that the two renderings match: they are irreducibly different, and pretending otherwise would promise portability the model cannot deliver. The assertion is that EVERY difference between them is one media.json or signal.json already predicted. A difference the data accounts for is the model working; a difference it does not account for is drift, and it fails the run.

cases.note: The hardest honest pair. Print was included in the medium enumeration precisely because it has no time and no interaction -- if the model survives print, it is real. Both channels are parallel, persistent and high-bandwidth, so a reading-and-comparing flow should cross almost intact, and every place it does not must be in the matrix.

cases.media_note: The pair that actually shipped. Both channels have a real implementation, so this is the only case where a divergence could be checked against running code rather than against a table.
cases.note: Serial versus parallel, transient versus persistent. SCAN, COMPARE, LOCATE and READ all degrade here, and muted renders as silence -- so this case exercises both matrices at once.
